.github/workflows/pg-ci.yml
1# GitHub Actions CI configuration for PostgreSQL
2#
3# For instructions on how to enable / disable CI integration in a repository
4# and further details, see src/tools/ci/README
5#
6# https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax
7# is a good starting point for documentation about GitHub Actions.
8
9name: CI for PostgreSQL
10
11on:
12  push:
13  # TODO: It might make sense to also add PR based triggers, to make it easier
14  # to use PRs on one's own repo, but it's a tad more complicated than just
15  # adding the 'pull_request' event, as naively doing so would often lead to
16  # running CI twice.
17
18# Restrict GITHUB_TOKEN to the minimum the jobs need: reading repo
19# contents during checkout.
20permissions:
21  contents: read
22
23concurrency:
24  # For anything other than stable branches, we want there to only be one
25  # workflow active for that branch. But on stable branches & master, we
26  # neither want to wait for prior runs, nor to cancel them, so that each
27  # separately pushed commit is tested.  We achieve that by setting a unique
28  # concurrency group when on such a branch.
29  group: |
30    ${{github.workflow }}-${{
31    case(github.ref == 'refs/heads/master' ||
32         (startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/heads/REL_') && endsWith(github.ref, '_STABLE')),
33         github.run_id,
34         github.ref)
35    }}
36  cancel-in-progress: true
37
38env:
39  # The lower depth accelerates git clone. Use a bit of depth so that
40  # concurrent jobs and retrying older runs have a chance of working.
41  CLONE_DEPTH: 500
42
43  # At the moment all jobs use 4vcore runners, and none seems to benefit from
44  # increasing concurrency further.
45  BUILD_JOBS: 4
46
47  # It's possible that some jobs benefit from an increased test concurrency,
48  # but a default of 4 is a safe bet. Individual jobs can override.
49  TEST_JOBS: 4
50
51  CCACHE_MAXSIZE: "250M"
52  CCACHE_DIR: ${{ github.workspace }}/ccache_dir
53
54  # Check target for the autoconf builds. Can be set to e.g. check to only
55  # test the main regression tests.
56  CHECK: check-world PROVE_FLAGS=--timer
57  CHECKFLAGS: -Otarget
58
59  # Build test dependencies as part of the build step, to see compiler
60  # errors/warnings in one place.
61  MBUILD_TARGET: all testprep
62  MTEST_ARGS: --print-errorlogs --no-rebuild -C build
63
64  # Can be set to a non-empty value to run a limited set of tests
65  # (e.g. --suite regress to only run the main regression tests).
66  MTEST_TARGET:
67
68  PGCTLTIMEOUT: 120  # avoids spurious failures during parallel tests
69  TEMP_CONFIG: ${{ github.workspace }}/src/tools/ci/pg_ci_base.conf
70  PG_TEST_EXTRA: kerberos ldap ssl libpq_encryption load_balance oauth
71
72  # Postgres config args for the meson builds, shared between all meson tasks
73  # except the 'SanityCheck' task
74  MESON_COMMON_PG_CONFIG_ARGS: -Dcassert=true -Dinjection_points=true
75
76  # Meson feature flags shared by all meson tasks, except:
77  # SanityCheck: uses almost no dependencies.
78  # Windows - VS: has fewer dependencies than listed here, so defines its own.
79  # Linux: uses the 'auto' feature option to test meson feature autodetection.
80  MESON_COMMON_FEATURES: >-
81    -Dauto_features=disabled
82    -Ddocs=enabled
83    -Dicu=enabled
84    -Dldap=enabled
85    -Dlibxml=enabled
86    -Dlibxslt=enabled
87    -Dlz4=enabled
88    -Dplperl=enabled
89    -Dplpython=enabled
90    -Dpltcl=enabled
91    -Dreadline=enabled
92    -Dssl=openssl
93    -Dtap_tests=enabled
94    -Dzlib=enabled
95    -Dzstd=enabled
96
97  # Shared between the Linux autoconf job and the CompilerWarnings jobs
98  LINUX_CONFIGURE_FEATURES: >-
99    --with-gssapi
100    --with-icu
101    --with-ldap
102    --with-libcurl
103    --with-libxml
104    --with-libxslt
105    --with-llvm
106    --with-lz4
107    --with-pam
108    --with-perl
109    --with-python
110    --with-selinux
111    --with-ssl=openssl
112    --with-systemd
113    --with-tcl --with-tclconfig=/usr/lib/tcl8.6/
114    --with-uuid=ossp
115    --with-zstd
116
117  # Centrally define the version of linux runners, to make it easier to
118  # update. We don't just want to use ubuntu-latest, as it's not implausible
119  # there will be breakage when that switches to the next ubuntu version.
120  _LINUX_RUNS_ON: &linux_runs_on |
121    ubuntu-24.04
122
123  # Debian Trixie containers used by all Linux jobs. Built by
124  # 'https://github.com/anarazel/pg-vm-images/'.
125  CONTAINER_REPO: ghcr.io/anarazel/pg-vm-images/main
126  CONTAINER_LINUX_CI: linux_debian_trixie_ci:latest
127  CONTAINER_LINUX_CI_DOCS: linux_debian_trixie_ci_docs:latest
128
129  # The full set of OS / job selectors recognized by the `ci-os-only:`
130  # commit-message directive parsed in the `setup` job below.
131  CI_OS_ONLY_JOBS: "linux macos windows mingw compilerwarnings sanitycheck"
132
133  ###
134  # A few variables to make expressions later on shorter
135  ###
136
137  ON_DEFAULT_BRANCH: ${{github.event.repository.default_branch == github.ref_name }}
138
139  # Note that we need to be careful to use a separator that can't be in branch
140  # names, otherwise e.g. caches for 'master' might be restored on the
141  # 'master-pending' branch.
142  CACHE_PREFIX_DEFAULT: >-
143    :${{ github.job }}:${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}:
144  CACHE_PREFIX_BRANCH: >-
145    :${{ github.job }}:${{ github.ref_name }}:
146  CACHE_SUFFIX: >-
147    ${{ github.run_id }}:${{ github.run_attempt }}
148
149
150jobs:
151
152  # Job: Report if repository has not opted into CI
153  #
154  # Do not run CI unless the repository owner opts in, to avoid resource waste
155  # in all the forks of postgres (new forks have workflows disabled by
156  # default, but old ones don't). Unfortunately there's no declarative way to
157  # do so.
158  #
159  # To make the lack of actual CI due to missing opt-in more visible, emit a
160  # summary explaining how CI can be opted into and how the entire workflow,
161  # including this warning, can be disabled.
162  warn-if-not-opted-in:
163    name: Report if not opted into CI
164    if: ${{vars.PG_CI_ENABLED != '1'}}
165    runs-on: ubuntu-slim
166    steps:
167      - name: Warn
168        env:
169          MSG: |
170            > [!IMPORTANT]
171            > ${{github.workflow}} has not been opted into in this repository
172            >
173            > To opt into ${{github.workflow}}, go to
174            > ${{github.server_url}}/${{github.repository}}/settings/variables/actions
175            > and create a new repository variable named PG_CI_ENABLED, with
176            > the value 1.
177            >
178            > To avoid seeing this message over and over, go to
179            > ${{github.server_url}}/${{github.repository}}/actions/workflows/pg-ci.yml
180            > and click on the three dots at the top right and choose
181            > "Disable workflow"
182        run: |
183          echo "$MSG" |tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
184
185
186  # Job: Determine enabled jobs
187  #
188  # Parses "ci-os-only: ..." from the commit message and exposes flags
189  # consumed by the jobs' `if:` conditions.
190  setup:
191    name: Determine enabled jobs
192    # Only run CI if repo owner opted in. If this task is skipped due to the
193    # if, none of it's depending tasks (i.e. the actual CI tasks) run either.
194    if: ${{vars.PG_CI_ENABLED == '1'}}
195    runs-on: *linux_runs_on
196    timeout-minutes: 1
197    outputs:
198      linux: ${{ steps.os.outputs.linux }}
199      macos: ${{ steps.os.outputs.macos }}
200      windows: ${{ steps.os.outputs.windows }}
201      mingw: ${{ steps.os.outputs.mingw }}
202      compilerwarnings: ${{ steps.os.outputs.compilerwarnings }}
203      sanitycheck: ${{ steps.os.outputs.sanitycheck }}
204      # Re-export workflow-level env vars that other jobs need to reference
205      # from contexts (e.g. `jobs.<id>.container.image`) where the `env`
206      # context is not available.
207      container_linux_ci: ${{ env.CONTAINER_REPO }}/${{ env.CONTAINER_LINUX_CI }}
208      container_linux_ci_docs: ${{ env.CONTAINER_REPO }}/${{ env.CONTAINER_LINUX_CI_DOCS }}
209
210    steps:
211      # Anchor reused by other jobs further down. GitHub Actions supports YAML
212      # anchors/aliases but not merge keys, so the alias copies the whole step
213      # verbatim. The anchor is resolved at YAML parse time, so the alias
214      # keeps working even if this job were to be skipped at runtime.
215      - &nix_sysinfo_step
216        name: sysinfo
217        run: |
218          id
219          uname -a
220          ulimit -a -H && ulimit -a -S
221          env
222
223      - name: Parse ci-os-only
224        id: os
225        env:
226          MSG: ${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}
227        shell: bash
228        run: |
229          all_os=${CI_OS_ONLY_JOBS}
230          if printf '%s\n' "$MSG" | grep -qE '^ci-os-only: '; then
231            sel=$(printf '%s\n' "$MSG" | sed -n 's/^ci-os-only: //p' | head -n 1)
232            echo "ci-os-only selection: $sel"
233          else
234            sel="$all_os"
235          fi
236          for o in $all_os; do
237            if echo " $sel " | grep -qE "[ ,]$o[ ,]"; then
238              echo "$o=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
239            else
240              echo "$o=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
241            fi
242          done
243          cat "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
244
245
246  # Job: SanityCheck
247  #
248  # To avoid unnecessarily spinning up a lot of VMs / containers for entirely
249  # broken commits, have a minimal task that all others depend on.
250  #
251  # SPECIAL:
252  # - Builds with --auto-features=disabled and thus almost no enabled
253  #   dependencies
254  sanity-check:
255    name: SanityCheck
256    needs: setup
257    if: |
258      !cancelled() &&
259      needs.setup.outputs.sanitycheck == 'true'
260    runs-on: *linux_runs_on
261    timeout-minutes: 15
262    container: &linux_ci_container
263      image: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.container_linux_ci }}
264
265      # Options passed to all linux containers. Not all of the jobs need
266      # all of them, but it's easier to just define them centrally.
267      #
268      # --privileged is needed so the prepare step can write to sysctls
269      # under /proc/sys (it's mounted read-only without it). We use it to
270      # set kernel.core_pattern and (for the meson entries) to flip
271      # kernel.io_uring_disabled (default 2 on recent GH runner kernels).
272      #
273      # Share the host PID + IPC namespaces. 017_shm.pl rapidly creates,
274      # kill9's, and restarts postgres; with the container's small PID
275      # space a new postgres can recycle the dead postmaster's PID before
276      # pg_ctl's postmaster.pid check notices, producing spurious "node X
277      # is already running" failures. SysV shm in the test also relies on
278      # host-like IPC behavior.
279      #
280      # --ulimit raises memlock and core dump size. Memlock is needed for
281      # running the AIO tests.
282      options: &linux_container_options |
283        --privileged --pid=host --ipc=host --ulimit memlock=-1:-1
284    env:
285      # no options enabled, should be small
286      CCACHE_MAXSIZE: "150M"
287
288    steps:
289      - *nix_sysinfo_step
290
291      - &checkout_step
292        uses: actions/checkout@v6
293        with:
294          fetch-depth: ${{ env.CLONE_DEPTH }}
295
296      # We restore both the ccache from the default branch (typically master),
297      # and from the current branch. This will often allow feature branches to
298      # start out with a high cache hit ratio.
299      #
300      # With ccache it turns out to work to just restore two caches into the
301      # same directory, as it's basically a content addressed store. Stats
302      # could be corrupted, but we zero them out anyway.
303      - &ccache_restore_default_step
304        name: "ccache: Restore for default branch ${{github.event.repository.default_branch}}"
305        if: ${{ env.ON_DEFAULT_BRANCH == 'false' }}
306        uses: actions/cache/restore@v5
307        with:
308          path: ${{ env.CCACHE_DIR }}
309          key: ccache${{env.CACHE_PREFIX_DEFAULT}}${{env.CACHE_SUFFIX}}
310          restore-keys: ccache${{env.CACHE_PREFIX_DEFAULT}}
311
312      - &ccache_restore_branch_step
313        name: "ccache: Restore for branch ${{ github.ref_name }}"
314        id: ccache-restore-branch
315        uses: actions/cache/restore@v5
316        with:
317          path: ${{ env.CCACHE_DIR }}
318          key: ccache${{env.CACHE_PREFIX_BRANCH}}${{env.CACHE_SUFFIX}}
319          restore-keys: ccache${{env.CACHE_PREFIX_BRANCH}}
320
321      - &linux_prepare_workspace_step
322        name: Prepare workspace
323        run: |
324          useradd -m postgres
325          chown -R postgres:postgres .
326          mkdir -m 770 /tmp/cores
327          chown root:postgres /tmp/cores
328          sysctl kernel.core_pattern='/tmp/cores/%e-%s-%p.core'
329          # This is only needed for some of the tasks using this, but it
330          # doesn't harm to have this enabled.
331          sysctl -w kernel.io_uring_disabled=0
332
333          cat >> /etc/hosts <<-EOF
334            127.0.0.1 pg-loadbalancetest
335            127.0.0.2 pg-loadbalancetest
336            127.0.0.3 pg-loadbalancetest
337          EOF
338
339      # By using a shell that includes su, the run commands themselves get
340      # simpler. As there are quite a few commands that need to use su...
341      - name: Configure
342        shell: &su_postgres_shell |
343          su postgres -c "bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail {0}"
344        run: |
345          meson setup \
346            --buildtype=debug \
347            --auto-features=disabled \
348            -Ddefault_library=shared \
349            -Dtap_tests=enabled \
350            build
351
352      - name: Build
353        shell: *su_postgres_shell
354        run: &ninja_build_cmd |
355          ninja -C build -j${{env.BUILD_JOBS}} ${{env.MBUILD_TARGET}}
356          ninja -C build -t missingdeps
357
358      # Decide if it's worth uploading a new version of the ccache cache. If
359      # we always do so unconditionally, we'd very quickly go through the
360      # allowed cache space. Instead we check if the hit rate is high enough
361      # already for that not to be worth it.
362      - &ccache_decide_save_step
363        name: "ccache: Decide whether to upload"
364        id: ccache-decide
365        # Make the decision whether to upload whenever the cache has been set
366        # up, so that incrementally addressing compiler errors/warnings
367        # doesn't have to start from scratch.
368        if: |
369          always() &&
370          steps.ccache-restore-branch.conclusion == 'success'
371        run: python3 src/tools/ci/gha_ccache_decide.py
372
373      - &ccache_save_step
374        name: "ccache: Upload cache"
375        uses: actions/cache/save@v5
376        if: |
377          always() &&
378          steps.ccache-decide.outputs.should_save == 'true'
379        with:
380          path: ${{ env.CCACHE_DIR }}
381          key: ${{ steps.ccache-restore-branch.outputs.cache-primary-key }}
382
383      # Run a minimal set of tests. The main regression tests take too long
384      # for this purpose. For now this is a random quick pg_regress style
385      # test, and a tap test that exercises both a frontend binary and the
386      # backend.
387      #
388      # To allow the command below to be reused by later tasks, we allow
389      # adding "setup" commands to be specified via the ADDITIONAL_SETUP
390      # environment variable.
391      #
392      # Note that this command is used on all platforms, therefore one needs
393      # to be careful about using only ${{env.}} variable references,
394      # linebreaks etc.
395      - name: Test
396        shell: *su_postgres_shell
397        env:
398          MTEST_TARGET: cube/regress pg_ctl/001_start_stop
399        run: &meson_test_world_cmd |
400          ${{case(runner.os == 'Windows', '', 'ulimit -c unlimited')}}
401
402          ${{env.ADDITIONAL_SETUP}}
403
404          echo ::group::test_setup
405          meson test ${{env.MTEST_ARGS}} --suite setup --logbase setup || exit 1
406          echo ::endgroup::
407
408          meson test ${{env.MTEST_ARGS}} --num-processes ${{env.TEST_JOBS}} --no-suite setup ${{env.MTEST_TARGET}}
409
410      - &linux_collect_cores_step
411        name: Core backtraces
412        if: failure() && !cancelled()
413        run: src/tools/ci/cores_backtrace.sh linux /tmp/cores
414
415      # Note that this is used for both meson and autoconf builds
416      - &upload_logs_step
417        name: Upload logs
418        if: failure() && !cancelled()
419        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
420        with:
421          name: logs-${{ github.job }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
422          path: |
423              **/*.log
424              **/*.diffs
425              **/regress_log_*
426              **/crashlog-*.txt
427              build/meson-logs/**
428              **/config.log
429          if-no-files-found: ignore
430
431
432  # Job: Linux - Autoconf
433  #
434  # SPECIAL:
435  # - Uses undefined & alignment sanitizers (sanitizer failures are typically
436  #   printed in the server log)
437  # - Configures postgres with a small segment size
438  # - Uses PG_TEST_PG_COMBINEBACKUP_MODE=--copy-file-range
439  # - Uses postgres specific CPPFLAGS that increase test coverage
440  # - Enables --link for pg_upgrade
441  linux-autoconf:
442    name: Linux - Autoconf
443    needs: [setup, sanity-check]
444    if: &linux_job_if |
445      !cancelled() &&
446      needs.setup.outputs.linux == 'true' &&
447      needs.sanity-check.result != 'failure'
448    runs-on: *linux_runs_on
449    container: *linux_ci_container
450    timeout-minutes: 60
451
452    env: &linux_env
453      # Add both debian and ubuntu, as symbols from the host can be visible during profiling
454      DEBUGINFOD_URLS: "https://debuginfod.debian.net https://debuginfod.ubuntu.com"
455      # Use -O2 to reduce the test times, use -fno-sanitize-recover=all to make sanitizer test
456      # failures visible.
457      CFLAGS: -O2 -ggdb -fno-sanitize-recover=all
458      CXXFLAGS: -O2 -ggdb -fno-sanitize-recover=all
459      LDFLAGS:
460      CC: ccache gcc
461      CXX: ccache g++
462      CLANG: ccache clang
463
464      # Configure sanitizer runtime behavior to be suitable for running tests:
465      # disable_coredump=0, abort_on_error=1: for useful backtraces in case of crashes
466      # print_stacktraces=1,verbosity=2, duh
467      # detect_leaks=0: too many uninteresting leak errors in short-lived binaries
468      UBSAN_OPTIONS: print_stacktrace=1:disable_coredump=0:abort_on_error=1:verbosity=2
469      ASAN_OPTIONS: print_stacktrace=1:disable_coredump=0:abort_on_error=1:detect_leaks=0
470
471    steps:
472      # GitHub Actions does not make it easy to share some, but not all,
473      # environment variables between related tasks. We solve that for the
474      # linux- tasks by updating the environment variables programmatically.
475      - name: Update Environment
476        env:
477          SANITIZER_FLAGS: -fsanitize=alignment,undefined
478          PG_TEST_PG_COMBINEBACKUP_MODE: --copy-file-range
479          CPPFLAGS: -DRELCACHE_FORCE_RELEASE -DENFORCE_REGRESSION_TEST_NAME_RESTRICTIONS
480          PG_TEST_PG_UPGRADE_MODE: --link
481        run: &linux_update_config_cmd |
482          echo "CPPFLAGS=$CPPFLAGS" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
483          echo "CFLAGS=$CFLAGS ${SANITIZER_FLAGS}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
484          echo "CXXFLAGS=$CXXFLAGS ${SANITIZER_FLAGS}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
485          echo "LDFLAGS=$LDFLAGS ${SANITIZER_FLAGS}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
486
487          echo "CC=${CC}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
488          echo "CXX=${CXX}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
489
490          echo "PG_TEST_PG_UPGRADE_MODE=${PG_TEST_PG_UPGRADE_MODE}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
491          echo "PG_TEST_INITDB_EXTRA_OPTS=${PG_TEST_INITDB_EXTRA_OPTS}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
492          echo "PG_TEST_PG_COMBINEBACKUP_MODE=${PG_TEST_PG_COMBINEBACKUP_MODE}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
493
494      - *nix_sysinfo_step
495      - *checkout_step
496      - *ccache_restore_default_step
497      - *ccache_restore_branch_step
498      - *linux_prepare_workspace_step
499
500      - name: Configure
501        shell: *su_postgres_shell
502        run: |
503          ./configure \
504            --enable-cassert --enable-injection-points --enable-debug \
505            --enable-tap-tests --enable-nls \
506            --with-segsize-blocks=6 \
507            --with-libnuma \
508            --with-liburing \
509            ${LINUX_CONFIGURE_FEATURES}
510
511      - name: Build
512        shell: *su_postgres_shell
513        run: |
514          make -s -j${BUILD_JOBS} world-bin
515
516      - *ccache_decide_save_step
517      - *ccache_save_step
518
519      - name: Test world
520        shell: *su_postgres_shell
521        run: |
522          make -s ${CHECK} ${CHECKFLAGS} -j${TEST_JOBS}
523
524      - *linux_collect_cores_step
525      - *upload_logs_step
526
527
528  # Job: Linux - Meson (32-bit)
529  #
530  # SPECIAL:
531  # - Uses undefined behaviour and alignment sanitizers, (sanitizer failures
532  #   are typically printed in the server log)
533  # - Uses io_method=io_uring
534  # - Uses meson feature autodetection
535  # - tests with LANG=C to give ICU some buildfarm-uncovered coverage. Also,
536  #   newer Python insists on changing LC_CTYPE away from C, prevent that with
537  #   PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE.
538  linux-meson-32:
539    name: Linux - Meson (32-bit)
540    needs: [setup, sanity-check]
541    if: *linux_job_if
542    runs-on: *linux_runs_on
543    container: *linux_ci_container
544    timeout-minutes: 60
545    env: *linux_env
546
547    steps:
548      - name: Update Environment
549        env:
550          SANITIZER_FLAGS: -fsanitize=alignment,undefined
551          PG_TEST_INITDB_EXTRA_OPTS: -c io_method=io_uring
552          CC: ccache gcc -m32
553          CXX: ccache g++ -m32
554        run: *linux_update_config_cmd
555
556      - *nix_sysinfo_step
557      - *checkout_step
558      - *ccache_restore_default_step
559      - *ccache_restore_branch_step
560      - *linux_prepare_workspace_step
561
562      - name: Configure
563        shell: *su_postgres_shell
564        run: |
565          meson setup \
566            ${MESON_COMMON_PG_CONFIG_ARGS} \
567            -Duuid=e2fs \
568            --buildtype=debug \
569            --pkg-config-path /usr/lib/i386-linux-gnu/pkgconfig/ \
570            -DPERL=perl5.40-i386-linux-gnu \
571            -Dlibnuma=disabled \
572            build
573
574      - name: Build
575        shell: *su_postgres_shell
576        run: *ninja_build_cmd
577
578      - *ccache_decide_save_step
579      - *ccache_save_step
580
581      - name: Test world
582        shell: *su_postgres_shell
583        env:
584          PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE: 0
585          LANG: C
586        run: *meson_test_world_cmd
587
588      # Test running against existing PG instance.
589      #
590      # linux-meson-32 chosen because it's currently comparatively fast
591      - name: Test running
592        shell: *su_postgres_shell
593        run: |
594          ulimit -c unlimited
595
596          # Ensure install exists, in case somebody is debugging a failing
597          # test and reorders this to be before "Test world".
598          echo ::group::test_setup
599          meson test ${{env.MTEST_ARGS}} --suite setup --logbase setup
600          echo ::endgroup::
601
602          # Make libraries discoverable (the x86_64 reference is a meson
603          # oddity)
604          export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$(pwd)/build/tmp_install/usr/local/pgsql/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH"
605
606          build/tmp_install/usr/local/pgsql/bin/initdb -N build/runningcheck --no-instructions -A trust
607          echo "include '$(pwd)/src/tools/ci/pg_ci_base.conf'" >> build/runningcheck/postgresql.conf
608
609          # Log into a place that will be archived in case of failure
610          mkdir -p build/testrun
611          build/tmp_install/usr/local/pgsql/bin/pg_ctl -c -o '-c fsync=off' -D build/runningcheck -l build/testrun/runningcheck.log start
612
613          # Run the tests supporting running against an already running
614          meson test ${{env.MTEST_ARGS}} --num-processes ${{env.TEST_JOBS}} --setup running
615
616          build/tmp_install/usr/local/pgsql/bin/pg_ctl -D build/runningcheck stop
617
618      - *linux_collect_cores_step
619      - *upload_logs_step

622  # Linux - Meson (64-bit)
623  #
624  # SPECIAL:
625  # - Uses address sanitizer, (sanitizer failures are typically printed in the
626  #   server log). We test asan with meson rather than autoconf, as it's a bit
627  #   faster at running the tests.
628  # - Uses io_method=io_uring
629  # - Uses meson feature autodetection
630  linux-meson-64:
631    name: Linux - Meson (64-bit)
632    needs: [setup, sanity-check]
633    if: *linux_job_if
634    runs-on: *linux_runs_on
635    container: *linux_ci_container
636    timeout-minutes: 60
637    env: *linux_env
638
639    steps:
640      - name: Update Environment
641        env:
642          SANITIZER_FLAGS: -fsanitize=address
643          PG_TEST_INITDB_EXTRA_OPTS: -c io_method=io_uring
644        run: *linux_update_config_cmd
645
646      - *nix_sysinfo_step
647      - *checkout_step
648      - *ccache_restore_default_step
649      - *ccache_restore_branch_step
650      - *linux_prepare_workspace_step
651
652      - name: Configure
653        shell: *su_postgres_shell
654        run: |
655          meson setup \
656            ${MESON_COMMON_PG_CONFIG_ARGS} \
657            -Duuid=e2fs \
658            --buildtype=debug \
659            -Dllvm=enabled \
660            build
661
662      - name: Build
663        shell: *su_postgres_shell
664        run: *ninja_build_cmd
665
666      - *ccache_decide_save_step
667      - *ccache_save_step

669      - name: Test world

677  # Job: macOS - Meson
678  #
679  # SPECIAL:
680  # - Enables --clone for pg_upgrade and pg_combinebackup
681  # - Specifies configuration options that test reading/writing/copying of node trees
682  # - Specifies debug_parallel_query=regress, to catch related issues during CI
683  macos:
684    name: macOS - Meson
685    needs: [setup, sanity-check]
686    if: |
687      !cancelled() &&
688      needs.setup.outputs.macos == 'true' &&
689      needs.sanity-check.result != 'failure'
690    runs-on: macos-15
691    timeout-minutes: 60
692    env:
693      MACPORTS_CACHE: ${{ github.workspace }}/macports-cache
694
695      MESON_FEATURES: >-
696        -Dbonjour=enabled
697        -Ddtrace=enabled
698        -Dgssapi=enabled
699        -Dlibcurl=enabled
700        -Dnls=enabled
701        -Duuid=e2fs
702
703      MACOS_PACKAGE_LIST: >-
704        ccache
705        icu
706        kerberos5
707        lz4
708        meson
709        openldap
710        openssl
711        p5.34-io-tty
712        p5.34-ipc-run
713        python312
714        tcl
715        zstd
716
717      CC: ccache cc
718      CXX: ccache c++
719      CFLAGS: -Og -ggdb
720      CXXFLAGS: -Og -ggdb
721      PG_TEST_PG_UPGRADE_MODE: --clone
722      PG_TEST_PG_COMBINEBACKUP_MODE: --clone
723
724      # Several buildfarm animals enable these options. Without testing them
725      # during CI, it would be easy to cause breakage on the buildfarm with CI
726      # passing.
727      PG_TEST_INITDB_EXTRA_OPTS: >-
728        -c debug_copy_parse_plan_trees=on
729        -c debug_write_read_parse_plan_trees=on
730        -c debug_raw_expression_coverage_test=on
731        -c debug_parallel_query=regress
732
733    steps:
734      - *nix_sysinfo_step
735      - *checkout_step
736
737      - name: Setup core files
738        run: |
739          mkdir -p $HOME/cores
740          sudo sysctl kern.corefile="$HOME/cores/core.%P"
741
742      - name: "Macports: Compute cache key"
743        id: mp-key
744        run: |
745          macos_major=$(sw_vers -productVersion | sed 's/\..*//')
746          pkglist_hash=$(printf '%s' "$MACOS_PACKAGE_LIST" | md5 -q)
747          script_hash=$(md5 -q src/tools/ci/ci_macports_packages.sh)
748          echo "key=macports-${macos_major}-${pkglist_hash}-${script_hash}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
749          # It's faster to start with a partial cache for the same macos
750          # version than from scratch
751          echo "restore-key=macports-${macos_major}-" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
752
753      - name: "MacPorts: Restore cache"
754        id: mp-restore
755        uses: actions/cache/restore@v5
756        with:
757          path: ${{ env.MACPORTS_CACHE }}
758          key: ${{ steps.mp-key.outputs.key }}
759          restore-keys: ${{ steps.mp-key.outputs.restore-key }}
760
761      # Use MacPorts, even though Homebrew is installed. The installation
762      # of the additional packages we need would take quite a while with
763      # Homebrew, even if we cache the downloads. We can't cache all of
764      # Homebrew, because it's already large. So we use MacPorts. To cache
765      # the installation we create a .dmg file that we mount if it already
766      # exists.
767      # XXX: The reason for the direct p5.34* references is that we'd need
768      # the large MacPort tree around to figure out that p5-io-tty is
769      # actually p5.34-io-tty. Using the unversioned name works, but
770      # updates MacPorts every time.
771      - name: "MacPorts: Install dependencies"
772        id: mp-install
773        env:
774          # Pass token so the script's GitHub API call to list MacPorts
775          # releases isn't subject to the 60/h/IP unauthenticated rate
776          # limit (shared across all jobs on the runner's IP).
777          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
778        run: |
779          sh src/tools/ci/ci_macports_packages.sh $MACOS_PACKAGE_LIST
780          # system python doesn't provide headers
781          sudo /opt/local/bin/port select python3 python312
782          # Make macports install visible to subsequent steps
783          echo /opt/local/sbin >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
784          echo /opt/local/bin >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
785
786      # Save macports before running build / tests, creating macports can be
787      # quite slow, so we don't want to start from scratch in the next run.
788      - name: "MacPorts: Save cache"
789        uses: actions/cache/save@v5
790        # Don't save cache if we had an exact match
791        if: |
792          steps.mp-install.conclusion == 'success' &&
793          steps.mp-restore.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
794        with:
795          path: ${{ env.MACPORTS_CACHE }}
796          key: ${{ steps.mp-key.outputs.key }}
797
798      - *ccache_restore_default_step
799      - *ccache_restore_branch_step
800
801      - name: Configure
802        env:
803          PKG_CONFIG_PATH: /opt/local/lib/pkgconfig/
804        run: |
805          meson setup \
806            ${{env.MESON_COMMON_PG_CONFIG_ARGS}} \
807            --buildtype=debug \
808            -Dextra_include_dirs=/opt/local/include \
809            -Dextra_lib_dirs=/opt/local/lib \
810            -Ddarwin_sysroot=none \
811            ${MESON_COMMON_FEATURES} \
812            ${MESON_FEATURES} \
813            build
814
815      - name: Build
816        run: *ninja_build_cmd
817
818      - *ccache_decide_save_step
819      - *ccache_save_step
820
821      - name: Test world
822        env:
823          # default is 256, pretty low
824          ADDITIONAL_SETUP: ulimit -n 1024
825        run: *meson_test_world_cmd
826
827      - name: Core backtraces
828        if: failure() && !cancelled()
829        run: src/tools/ci/cores_backtrace.sh macos "$HOME/cores"
830
831      - *upload_logs_step

834  # Job: Windows - Visual Studio
835  #
836  # If we were to execute tests in this job serially, this would be the
837  # slowest job by a good margin. To avoid that, use a matrix in combination
838  # with meson test's --slice SLICE/NUM_SLICES mechanism to split the tests
839  # across two runners.
840  windows-vs:
841    name: Windows - Visual Studio - Slice ${{ matrix.slice}}/${{ matrix.num_slices}}
842    needs: [setup, sanity-check]
843    if: |
844      !cancelled() &&
845      needs.setup.outputs.windows == 'true' &&
846      needs.sanity-check.result != 'failure'
847    runs-on: windows-2022
848    timeout-minutes: 60
849
850    # As described at the top of the task, split the tests across two runners
851    # for performance. The gains from additional concurrency diminish
852    # relatively quickly, due to each instance having to install dependencies
853    # and build postgres.
854    strategy:
855      fail-fast: false
856      matrix:
857        num_slices: [2]
858        slice: [1, 2]
859
860    env:
861      # Avoid port conflicts between concurrent tap tests
862      PG_TEST_USE_UNIX_SOCKETS: 1
863      PG_REGRESS_SOCK_DIR: 'd:\pgsock'
864      TAR: "c:/windows/system32/tar.exe"
865
866      MESON_FEATURES: >-
867        -Dauto_features=disabled
868        -Dcpp_args=/std:c++20
869        -Dldap=enabled
870        -Dplperl=enabled
871        -Dplpython=enabled
872        -Dssl=openssl
873        -Dtap_tests=enabled
874
875    defaults:
876      run:
877        shell: cmd
878
879    steps:
880      - &windows_disable_defender_step
881        name: Disable Windows Defender
882        shell: pwsh
883        run: |
884          Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $true -SubmitSamplesConsent NeverSend -MAPSReporting Disable
885          # Verify Defender status
886          $status = Get-MpComputerStatus -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
887          if ($status) {
888              Write-Host "RealTimeProtectionEnabled: $($status.RealTimeProtectionEnabled)"
889              Write-Host "AntivirusEnabled: $($status.AntivirusEnabled)"
890          }
891
892      - *checkout_step
893
894      - name: Sysinfo
895        run: |
896          chcp
897          systeminfo
898          set
899
900      # The TAP tests build an initdb template under build/tmp_install and
901      # then `robocopy` it into per-test data directories. Robocopy with the
902      # default /COPY:DAT flag doesn't copy ACLs — destinations inherit from
903      # their parent dir. On GitHub-hosted Windows runners the workspace's
904      # inherited ACL grants Administrators:(F) and Users:(RX) but does NOT
905      # grant the runner user (runneradmin) directly. That matters because
906      # pg_ctl on Windows uses CreateRestrictedProcess to drop admin
907      # privileges from postmaster, so the postmaster process has the user
908      # SID in its token but no longer the Administrators group — leaving it
909      # with only "Users:(RX)" on pg_control and friends, which causes
910      # "PANIC: could not open file global/pg_control: Permission denied".
911      #
912      # Fix it once on the workspace dir with (OI)(CI) inheritance flags so
913      # every file/dir created underneath gets an explicit grant for the
914      # current user.
915      - name: Grant workspace ACL to runner user
916        shell: pwsh
917        run: |
918          icacls "${{ github.workspace }}" /grant "${env:USERNAME}:(OI)(CI)F" /Q | Out-Null
919          Write-Host "Granted Full Control to $env:USERNAME on ${{ github.workspace }}"
920
921      # postgres' plpython3u loads python3.dll (the stable-ABI forwarder)
922      # which in turn loads whichever python3NN.dll the Windows loader finds
923      # first on PATH. On windows-2022 `C:\Program Files\Mercurial\` ships
924      # its own python3.dll + python39.dll and appears on PATH *before* the
925      # hostedtoolcache Python 3.12 — so without intervention the backend
926      # ends up running Python 3.9 while postgres' stdlib search uses 3.12,
927      # producing `ImportError: cannot import name 'text_encoding' from
928      # 'io'` (the 3.12 `io.py` calling into 3.9's `_io`).
929      #
930      # Drop Mercurial's directory from PATH so the hostedtoolcache
931      # python3.dll wins the DLL search.
932      - name: Remove Mercurial from PATH
933        shell: pwsh
934        run: |
935          $filtered = ($env:PATH -split ';' |
936            Where-Object { $_ -and ($_ -notmatch '\\Mercurial\\?$') }) -join ';'
937          Add-Content $env:GITHUB_ENV "PATH=$filtered"
938          Write-Host "Removed Mercurial entries from PATH"
939
940      # Install some dependencies via msys64, that seems to be the fastest and
941      # most reliable
942      - name: Install dependencies, Mingw
943        shell: 'C:\msys64\usr\bin\bash.exe --login -eo pipefail "{0}"'
944        run: |
945          # Install some dependencies via msys64, that seems to be the fastest
946          # and most reliable
947          pacman -S --noconfirm --needed --asdeps \
948            bison flex
949
950          # Make bison and flex visible
951          echo C:/msys64/usr/bin >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
952
953          # Don't prefer mingw's perl
954          echo C:/Strawberry/perl/bin >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
955
956      - name: Install dependencies
957        shell: pwsh
958        run: |
959          # meson is not preinstalled on windows-2022. Install via pip
960          echo ::group::pip
961          python -m pip install --upgrade meson
962          if (!$?) { throw 'cmdfail' }
963          echo ::endgroup::
964
965          # Install IPC::Run.
966          # - recommends_policy=0 keeps cpan from pulling in IO::Tty / IO::Pty,
967          #   which don't build on Windows ("This module requires a POSIX
968          #   compliant system to work").
969          # - Pin to NJM/IPC-Run-20250809.0 because TODDR/IPC-Run-20260322.0
970          #   broke postgres tap tests on Windows (changed pipe stdio
971          #   handling). See upstream pg-vm-images commit ff5238afa3 and
972          #   the thread at
973          #   https://postgr.es/m/CAN55FZ06xanSbJdHe-CurjX_qNuBWZDEvS1kAk36L38YCtZXnw%40mail.gmail.com
974          echo ::group::cpan_ipc_run
975          "o conf recommends_policy 0`no conf commit`nnotest install NJM/IPC-Run-20250809.0.tar.gz" | cpan
976          if (!$?) { throw 'cmdfail' }
977          perl -mIPC::Run -e 1
978          if (!$?) { throw 'cmdfail' }
979          echo ::endgroup::
980
981      - &window_setup_hosts_step
982        name: Setup hosts file
983        shell: pwsh
984        run: |
985          Add-Content c:\Windows\System32\Drivers\etc\hosts "127.0.0.1 pg-loadbalancetest"
986          Add-Content c:\Windows\System32\Drivers\etc\hosts "127.0.0.2 pg-loadbalancetest"
987          Add-Content c:\Windows\System32\Drivers\etc\hosts "127.0.0.3 pg-loadbalancetest"
988
989      - name: Setup socket directory
990        shell: cmd
991        run: mkdir ${{env.PG_REGRESS_SOCK_DIR}}
992
993      - name: Configure
994        run: |
995          call "C:\Program Files\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\Enterprise\VC\Auxiliary\Build\vcvarsall.bat" x64
996          meson setup ^
997            --backend ninja ^
998            ${{env.MESON_COMMON_PG_CONFIG_ARGS}} ^
999            ${{env.MESON_FEATURES}} ^
1000            --buildtype debug ^
1001            -Db_pch=true ^
1002            -DTAR=${{env.TAR}} ^
1003            build
1004
1005      - name: Build
1006        run: |
1007          call "C:\Program Files\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\Enterprise\VC\Auxiliary\Build\vcvarsall.bat" x64
1008          ninja -C build ${{env.MBUILD_TARGET}} || exit 1
1009          ninja -C build -t missingdeps
1010
1011      - name: Test world
1012        env:
1013          # As described at the top of the task, split the tests across two
1014          # runners for performance.  It's not the prettiest to implement this
1015          # by prepending to MTEST_TARGET, but a more complicated solution
1016          # doesn't seem worth it.
1017          MTEST_TARGET: --slice ${{ matrix.slice}}/${{ matrix.num_slices}} ${{env.MTEST_TARGET}}
1018          ADDITIONAL_SETUP: |
1019            call "C:\Program Files\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\Enterprise\VC\Auxiliary\Build\vcvarsall.bat" x64
1020        run: *meson_test_world_cmd
1021
1022      # TODO: We need to collect crashlogs but for them to be generated, we'd
1023      # have to configure the JIT Debugger to do so. cdb.exe is installed on
1024      # the runner so that is possible.
1025      - *upload_logs_step
1026
1027
1028  # Job: Windows - MinGW - Meson
1029  windows-mingw:
1030    name: Windows - MinGW - Meson
1031    needs: [setup, sanity-check]
1032    if: |
1033      !cancelled() &&
1034      needs.setup.outputs.mingw == 'true' &&
1035      needs.sanity-check.result != 'failure'
1036    runs-on: windows-2022
1037    timeout-minutes: 60
1038    env:
1039      # Avoid port conflicts between concurrent tap tests
1040      PG_TEST_USE_UNIX_SOCKETS: 1
1041      PG_REGRESS_SOCK_DIR: 'd:\pgsock'
1042      TAR: "c:/windows/system32/tar.exe"
1043
1044      MSYS: winjitdebug
1045      CHERE_INVOKING: 1
1046      MSYSTEM: UCRT64
1047
1048      # Keep -Dnls explicitly disabled, as the number of files it creates
1049      # causes a noticeable slowdown.
1050      MESON_FEATURES: >-
1051        -Dnls=disabled
1052
1053      CCACHE_MAXSIZE: "500M"
1054      CCACHE_SLOPPINESS: pch_defines,time_macros
1055      CCACHE_DEPEND: 1
1056
1057    defaults:
1058      run:
1059        shell: 'D:\msys64\usr\bin\bash.exe --login -eo pipefail "{0}"'
1060
1061    steps:
1062      - *windows_disable_defender_step
1063      - *window_setup_hosts_step
1064      - *checkout_step
1065
1066      # Relocate the preinstalled MSYS2 tree from C:\ (slow system disk) to
1067      # D:\ (faster ephemeral data disk). Every subsequent MSYS2 step uses
1068      # D:\msys64\usr\bin\bash.exe via the job's `defaults.run.shell`.
1069      #
1070      # This reduces the total runtime of this task by ~15 minutes.
1071      #
1072      # robocopy returns 0-7 on success (with various "files copied" bits
1073      # set) and 8+ on real failure, so we have to translate its exit code.
1074      - name: Relocate MSYS2 to D
1075        shell: pwsh
1076        run: |
1077          robocopy C:\msys64 D:\msys64 /E /NJS /NJH /NFL /NDL /NP
1078          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ge 8) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }
1079          exit 0
1080
1081      - name: Setup MSYS2
1082        run: |
1083          # ${MINGW_PACKAGE_PREFIX} is an environment variable used in the
1084          # MSYS2. It dynamically expands to the correct prefix for the active
1085          # shell environment.
1086          pacman -S --noconfirm --needed  --asdeps \
1087            git bison flex diffutils \
1088            ${MINGW_PACKAGE_PREFIX}-ccache \
1089            ${MINGW_PACKAGE_PREFIX}-gcc \
1090            ${MINGW_PACKAGE_PREFIX}-icu \
1091            ${MINGW_PACKAGE_PREFIX}-libbacktrace \
1092            ${MINGW_PACKAGE_PREFIX}-libxml2 \
1093            ${MINGW_PACKAGE_PREFIX}-libxslt \
1094            ${MINGW_PACKAGE_PREFIX}-lz4 \
1095            ${MINGW_PACKAGE_PREFIX}-make \
1096            ${MINGW_PACKAGE_PREFIX}-meson \
1097            ${MINGW_PACKAGE_PREFIX}-perl \
1098            ${MINGW_PACKAGE_PREFIX}-pkgconf \
1099            ${MINGW_PACKAGE_PREFIX}-readline \
1100            ${MINGW_PACKAGE_PREFIX}-zlib \
1101            ${MINGW_PACKAGE_PREFIX}-zstd
1102
1103      - *nix_sysinfo_step
1104
1105      - name: Install additional dependencies
1106        run: |
1107          # Pin IPC::Run to NJM/IPC-Run-20250809.0; TODDR/IPC-Run-20260322.0
1108          # broke postgres tap tests on Windows (pipe stdio handling).
1109          # See pg-vm-images commit ff5238afa3.
1110          echo ::group::cpan_ipc_run
1111          (echo; echo o conf recommends_policy 0; echo notest install NJM/IPC-Run-20250809.0.tar.gz) | cpan
1112          perl -mIPC::Run -e 1
1113          echo ::endgroup::
1114
1115      - name: Setup socket directory
1116        shell: cmd
1117        run: mkdir ${{env.PG_REGRESS_SOCK_DIR}}
1118
1119      - *ccache_restore_default_step
1120      - *ccache_restore_branch_step
1121
1122      - name: Configure
1123        run: |
1124          meson setup \
1125            ${{env.MESON_COMMON_PG_CONFIG_ARGS}} \
1126            -Ddebug=true -Doptimization=g -Db_pch=true \
1127            ${{env.MESON_COMMON_FEATURES}} \
1128            ${{env.MESON_FEATURES}} \
1129            -DTAR=${{env.TAR}} \
1130            build
1131
1132      - name: Build
1133        run: *ninja_build_cmd
1134
1135      - *ccache_decide_save_step
1136      - *ccache_save_step
1137
1138      - name: Test world
1139        run: *meson_test_world_cmd
1140
1141      # TODO: We want to include crashlogs, but they are not yet
1142      # collected. cdb.exe is installed on the runner, so we can configure it
1143      # appropriately.
1144      - *upload_logs_step
1145
1146
1147  # Job: CompilerWarnings
1148  #
1149  # Test that code can be built with both gcc and clang without warnings,
1150  # with various combinations of cassert/dtrace flags. Trace probes have
1151  # a history of getting accidentally broken; the matrix is there to
1152  # catch that.
1153  #
1154  # The autoconf cache files (gcc.cache / clang.cache) are intentionally
1155  # reused across the matrix entries that share a compiler, so we don't
1156  # pay for full feature detection on every entry.
1157  compiler-warnings:
1158    name: CompilerWarnings
1159    needs: [setup, sanity-check]
1160    if: |
1161      !cancelled() &&
1162      needs.setup.outputs.compilerwarnings == 'true' &&
1163      needs.sanity-check.result != 'failure'
1164    runs-on: *linux_runs_on
1165    timeout-minutes: 60
1166    container:
1167      image: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.container_linux_ci_docs }}
1168    env:
1169      # Use larger ccache cache as this job compiles with multiple
1170      # compilers / flag combinations.
1171      CCACHE_MAXSIZE: "1G"
1172      DEFAULT_BUILD: world-bin
1173
1174    steps:
1175      - *nix_sysinfo_step
1176      - *checkout_step
1177      - *ccache_restore_default_step
1178      - *ccache_restore_branch_step
1179
1180      - name: Setup workspace
1181        run: |
1182          echo "COPT=-Werror" > src/Makefile.custom
1183
1184      # gcc, cassert off, dtrace on
1185      - name: gcc warnings + (dtrace)
1186        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
1187        env:
1188          CONF: ${{env.LINUX_CONFIGURE_FEATURES}} --cache gcc.cache --enable-dtrace
1189          CC: ccache gcc
1190          CXX: ccache g++
1191          CLANG: ccache clang
1192        run: &compiler_warnings_cmd |
1193          echo "::group::configure"
1194          ./configure \
1195            ${{env.CONF}} \
1196            CLANG="ccache clang"
1197          echo "::endgroup::"
1198
1199          make -s -j${{env.BUILD_JOBS}} clean
1200          make -s -j${{env.BUILD_JOBS}} ${{env.DEFAULT_BUILD}}
1201
1202      # gcc, cassert on, dtrace off
1203      - name: gcc warnings + (cassert)
1204        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
1205        env:
1206          CONF: ${{env.LINUX_CONFIGURE_FEATURES}} --cache gcc.cache --enable-cassert
1207          CC: ccache gcc
1208          CXX: ccache g++
1209        run: *compiler_warnings_cmd
1210
1211      # clang, cassert off, dtrace off
1212      - name: clang warnings
1213        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
1214        env:
1215          CONF: ${{env.LINUX_CONFIGURE_FEATURES}} --cache clang.cache
1216          CC: ccache clang
1217          CXX: ccache clang++
1218        run: *compiler_warnings_cmd
1219
1220      # clang, cassert on, dtrace on
1221      - name: clang warnings + (cassert + dtrace)
1222        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
1223        env:
1224          CONF: ${{env.LINUX_CONFIGURE_FEATURES}} --cache clang.cache --enable-cassert --enable-dtrace
1225          CC: ccache clang
1226          CXX: ccache clang++
1227        run: *compiler_warnings_cmd
1228
1229      - name: mingw warnings (cross compilation)
1230        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
1231        env:
1232          CONF: --host=x86_64-w64-mingw32ucrt --enable-cassert --without-icu
1233          CC: ccache x86_64-w64-mingw32ucrt-gcc
1234          CXX: ccache x86_64-w64-mingw32ucrt-g++
1235        run: *compiler_warnings_cmd
1236
1237      ###
1238      # Verify docs can be built
1239      ###
1240      # XXX: Only do this if there have been changes in doc/ since last build
1241      - name: Build documentation
1242        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
1243        env:
1244          CONF: --cache gcc.cache
1245          CC: ccache gcc
1246          CXX: ccache g++
1247          DEFAULT_BUILD: -C doc
1248        run: *compiler_warnings_cmd
1249
1250      ###
1251      # Verify headerscheck / cpluspluscheck succeed
1252      #
1253      # - Run both in same script to increase parallelism, use -k to get
1254      #   result of both
1255      # - Use -fmax-errors, as particularly cpluspluscheck can be very verbose
1256      ###
1257      - name: headerscheck + cpluspluscheck
1258        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
1259        run: |
1260          echo "::group::configure"
1261          ./configure \
1262            ${{env.LINUX_CONFIGURE_FEATURES}} \
1263            --cache gcc.cache \
1264            --quiet \
1265            CC="ccache gcc" CXX="ccache g++" CLANG="ccache clang"
1266          echo "::endgroup::"
1267
1268          make -s -j${{env.BUILD_JOBS}} clean
1269          make -s -j${{env.BUILD_JOBS}} -k ${{env.CHECKFLAGS}} \
1270            headerscheck cpluspluscheck \
1271            EXTRAFLAGS='-fmax-errors=10'
1272
1273      - *ccache_decide_save_step
1274      - *ccache_save_step
1275      - *upload_logs_step
